content: 1. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of tacrolimus by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4, which is responsible for its metabolism. Close monitoring is required when these drugs are co-administered. 2. Tetracycline increases the levels or effects of tadalafil by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution should be exercised, and close monitoring is recommended. 3. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of tamoxifen by inhibiting CYP3A4, which reduces the conversion of tamoxifen to its active metabolite, N-desmethyl tamoxifen. This interaction necessitates close monitoring. 4. Metronidazole increases the levels of tamsulosin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Dose adjustments may be necessary for drugs predominantly metabolized by CYP3A4. Close monitoring is advised. 5. Tazemetostat decreases the levels or effects of tetracycline by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative therapies should be considered due to the potential for significant interaction. 6. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of tazemetostat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. If unavoidable, tazemetostat dosage should be reduced, and close monitoring is required. 7. Tecovirimat decreases the levels or effects of tetracycline by weakly inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Sensitive CYP3A4 substrates should be monitored for effectiveness when co-administered. 8. Tetracycline decreases the effects of temocillin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Alternative drugs should be used, as this interaction is contraindicated. 9. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of temsirolimus by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. 10. Bismuth subsalicylate decreases the levels of tetracycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Alternative drugs should be used. 11. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of tezacaftor by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 12. Tetracycline increases the levels or effects of tezacaftor by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjustments to the tezacaftor dosage regimen are necessary when co-administered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 13. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of theophylline by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 14. Tetracycline decreases the levels or effects of thiamine by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. 15. Metronidazole decreases the levels or effects of thiamine by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. 16. Bismuth subsalicylate and timolol may cause severe hypertension due to pharmacodynamic synergism, specifically through the blockage of renal prostaglandin synthesis. Close monitoring is required. 17. Tetracycline increases the levels or effects of tinidazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Close monitoring is recommended. 18. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of tinidazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. 19. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of tipranavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 20. Inhaled tobramycin and bismuth subsalicylate both increase the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Concurrent or sequential use should be avoided to reduce the risk of ototoxicity. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 21. Tetracycline increases the levels of tofacitinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Dose adjustments may be necessary if co-administered with both moderate CYP3A4 and potent CYP2C19 inhibitors. 22. Metronidazole increases the levels of tofacitinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. Dose adjustments may be necessary if co-administered with both moderate CYP3A4 and potent CYP2C19 inhibitors. 23. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of tolterodine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are required. 24. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of tolvaptan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, and alternative drugs should be considered. 25. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of trabectedin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Close monitoring is necessary. 26. Tetracycline increases the levels or effects of trabectedin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 27. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of trazodone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are required. 28. Tetracycline and tretinoin increase each other's toxicity through an unspecified interaction mechanism. This combination is contraindicated. 29. Tetracycline and tretinoin increase phototoxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism. Alternative drugs should be used. 30. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of triamcinolone acetonide injectable suspension by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. 31. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of triazolam by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are required. 32. Trimagnesium citrate anhydrous decreases the levels of tetracycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Tetracycline should be administered at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after magnesium-containing products. 33. Tripotassium dicitrato bismuthate decreases the levels of tetracycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Alternative drugs should be used. 34. Tucatinib increases the levels or effects of tetracycline by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, and alternative drugs should be considered. 35. Tetracycline decreases the effects of the live typhoid vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. 36. Metronidazole decreases the effects of the live typhoid vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Administration of the live bacterial vaccine should be delayed until antibiotic therapy is completed. 37. Tetracycline increases the levels or effects of vardenafil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 38. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of vardenafil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 39. Tetracycline increases the effects of vecuronium through pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of respiratory depression. Alternative drugs should be used. 40. Tetracycline increases the levels or effects of venetoclax by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, and alternative drugs should be considered. If unavoidable, the venetoclax dose should be reduced by at least 50%. 41. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of venetoclax by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, and alternative drugs should be considered. If unavoidable, the venetoclax dose should be reduced by at least 50%. Close monitoring for signs of venetoclax toxicities is required. 42. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of verapamil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. 43. Tetracycline and verteporfin increase phototoxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 44. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of vinblastine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 45. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of vincristine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 46. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of liposomal vincristine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 47. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of vinorelbine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 48. Tetracycline increases the levels or effects of voclosporin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 49. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of voclosporin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 50. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of voriconazole by inhibiting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 51. Tetracycline increases the effects of warfarin through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Close monitoring is required. 52. Metronidazole increases the levels of warfarin through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. 53. Bismuth subsalicylate increases the effects of warfarin through anticoagulation. Co-administration should be avoided, and alternative drugs should be considered. 54. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of zaleplon by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 55. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of zanubrutinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Zanubrutinib dosage should be reduced to 80 mg twice daily when co-administered with a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor. 56. Tetracycline increases the levels or effects of zanubrutinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Zanubrutinib dosage should be reduced to 80 mg twice daily when co-administered with a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor. 57. Zinc decreases the levels or effects of tetracycline by cation binding in the gastrointestinal tract. Oral administration of tetracycline derivatives and zinc salts should be separated by at least 2 hours. 58. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of ziprasidone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 59. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of zolpidem by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 60. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of zonisamide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown.
